subject_line: A Tick Bite Could End Your Carnivore Diet
opening: Happy Sunday, friends. This week's lineup hit differently, and there's one story in particular that I think every carnivore needs to read before the weekend's out. We've also got a DIY trend taking over the forum and a quiet controversy brewing in the influencer space. Let's get into it.

hero.title: Alpha-Gal Syndrome: When a Tick Bite Ends Carnivore
hero.teaser: Imagine doing everything right on carnivore and then suddenly red meat starts making you sick. Not a little off, genuinely ill. That's exactly what's happening to people with alpha-gal syndrome, and the scary part is the tick bite that causes it can happen months before you notice a single symptom. Sarah breaks down how this immune response works, who's most at risk, and the specific signs that separate alpha-gal from a bad batch of beef. If you've had any unexplained reactions lately, you'll want to know this.

supporting.title: Everyone's Curing Their Own Bacon Now
supporting.teaser: Chloe found out why the DIY curing trend exploded in the forum this month, and there's one thing almost everyone getting started gets completely wrong.

supporting.title: Refilling Muscle Glycogen Without a Single Carb
supporting.teaser: Marcus says you can absolutely restock muscle glycogen on carnivore, but the timing piece most people skip is what makes or breaks the whole thing.

supporting.title: Why Carnivore Influencers Are Quietly Adding Plants
supporting.teaser: Some of the biggest names in the carnivore space are adding plants back in without making a big announcement, and the community's reaction is more complicated than you'd expect.

try_this_week: Do a quick tick exposure check. If you spend any time outdoors, think back over the last six months and look for any unexplained skin reactions, hives, or digestive flare-ups that showed up a few hours after eating red meat. If anything lines up, Sarah's article on alpha-gal gives you a clear list of symptoms to bring to your doctor. It takes five minutes and could save you a lot of confusion.
looking_ahead: Next week we're getting into something the community has strong opinions about, and the answer isn't as simple as either side wants it to be. Don't miss it.
